newsitem.title: INDIA: India copper loses ground, base metals ranged.
newsitem.headline: India copper loses ground, base metals ranged.

text.p: Copper prices lost the gained ground on the local market on Monday but other base metals were ranged, dealers said.
Copper moved down by 50 rupees at 13,875 rupees per quintal on demand resistance by industrial consumers while a setback in the world market prompted profit-taking. Copper was up 25 rupees last week.

Tin and nickel were steady at the reduced level on stray physical enquiries while the easing pressure of arrivals kept offerings at a low ebb. Tin was steady at 30,200 rupees after losing 700 rupees last week with nickel steady at 35,400 rupees per quintal after losing 800 rupees per quintal last week.

Zinc was indicated at the previous level of 8,100 rupees per quintal as was lead at 4,100 rupees and aluminium at 7,700 rupees per quintal in nominal activity. Zinc was up by 50 rupees per quintal last week.
